cases.purpose: A qualified, timely state-discriminating observation improves the owner-weighted loss after its declared cost.
An uninformative observation with zero acquisition cost must not be assigned positive decision value.
Waiting for an observation can make an otherwise feasible action miss its conservative completion window.
A source without rights for the requested use cannot enter the decision policy.
An observation with unqualified common-mode error treatment cannot improve action admissibility.
A candidate intervention without human approval remains unavailable.
A candidate intervention without its required resources remains unavailable.
A candidate intervention that breaches any declared hard service floor is not admissible.
An observation arriving at or after the decision deadline is not used for that decision.
Prior probability mass must sum exactly to one million parts per million.
An intervention with stale input evidence remains unavailable even when its physical model flag is otherwise admissible.
An intervention with unresolved owner or asset scope cannot be recommended.
A non-intervention HOLD fallback must remain representable when approval, resource, freshness and scope gates for interventions are closed.
A non-mutation abstention fallback remains representable when intervention physical-admissibility evidence is absent or false; its unserved-service loss is still scored.
